qt: to the Commission Matteo Gazzini (PPE) Subject:

The ECB's pursuit of a policy to increase interest rates has helped to mitigate inflation at a regulatory level. Nevertheless, given the downward trend in inflation, it is imperative to assess the relevance of maintaining interest rates at the current levels. Historically, high rates have been effective against inflation, but with inflation now under control, persisting with high rates could put a brake on economic activity and have an adverse effect on employment and social cohesion in the EU. Low interest rates are drivers of investment, which is essential for economic growth and generating employment. Lowering interest rates would also reduce loan repayments, making it easier for families to buy property. Can the Commission therefore clearly indicate what initiatives will be considered to persuade the ECB to reconsider – and possibly reduce – interest rates?

(9 April 2024) Regarding the Honourable Member’s concerns about the European Central Bank (ECB) monetary policy, the Commission would like to highlight that monetary policy is not a competence of the Commission. The design and the implementation of monetary policy in the euro area are the sole responsibility of the ECB and the national central banks of the Member States that have adopted the euro. Pursuant to Article 130 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the ECB is independent in the conduct of monetary policy in the euro area, and the Commission is under a legal duty to respect the ECB’s independence.
